name: Travel Health Checklist
description: A checklist for getting healthy and ready before a trip, from a doctor visit to medicines, insurance, and food safety.

sections.title: See Your Doctor or Travel Clinic

items.text: Book a visit four to six weeks before departure
Discuss your destination and planned activities
Ask about vaccines and any country requirements
Review how your conditions may be affected by travel
Get advice for high-altitude or remote destinations
items.note: Some preparation needs lead time, so book early

items.text: Pack enough of your regular medicines plus extra
Keep medicines in original labeled containers
Carry copies of your prescriptions
Split medicines between carry-on and checked bags
Check rules for carrying medicines at your destination
Arrange travel insurance with medical coverage
Confirm coverage for emergencies and existing conditions
Carry insurance details and emergency numbers
Keep copies of vaccination and medical records
Note the location of clinics or hospitals at your destination
Pack a compact travel first-aid kit
Include items for common travel ailments
Add sunscreen and insect protection if needed
Bring hand sanitizer and hygiene items
Carry rehydration supplies for stomach upsets

sections.title: Food, Water and On the Road

items.text: Check whether tap water is safe at your destination
Plan for bottled or treated water if needed
Follow safe food choices for the area
Stay hydrated and rest to adjust to time changes
Know the local emergency number before you go
items.note: For emergencies abroad, use the local emergency number

items.text: This checklist is general information only and is not medical advice; for vaccines, medicines, and destination-specific guidance, consult your doctor or a travel clinic and follow their recommendations
items.note: Check official travel health resources such as the CDC for your destination

faq.q: How far ahead should I prepare my health for travel?
faq.a: Start several weeks before departure, since some vaccines and prescriptions need lead time. Booking a doctor or travel clinic visit four to six weeks ahead gives you room to prepare properly.

faq.q: What medicines should I pack for a trip?
faq.a: Bring enough of your regular prescriptions for the whole trip plus extra, in their original labeled containers, with copies of prescriptions. Add basics like pain relief and items for common travel ailments your pharmacist suggests.

faq.q: Do I need travel insurance for health?
faq.a: Travel insurance that includes medical coverage is worth considering, especially abroad where care can be costly. Check what is covered, including emergencies and any pre-existing conditions, before you buy.

faq.q: How do I stay safe with food and water while traveling?
faq.a: Depending on the destination, you may need to choose bottled or treated water, avoid ice and raw foods, and eat freshly cooked items. Check destination guidance and ask your doctor or travel clinic.

faq.q: Is this travel health checklist printable?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF, work through it before you leave, and keep a copy with your travel documents and medicine bag.
